messages:
Ali: Heads-up — deploybot refused the staging->canary promote for release/2026.03.21. GCR attestation verify failed for eu-west1 :eyes:

deploy-bot: promotion blocked: provenance verification failed in eu-west1 mirror 
error="manifest digest mismatch for manifest list: platform entry ordering changed" 
refs=[gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321]

maya: ugh, saw similar once when buildx changed the manifestlist ordering. can you paste the deploybot log?

ben: pasting the key snippet from staging publish job logs — short: GCR rejects cosign verify because the signed manifest digest doesn't match the mirror's stored manifestlist digest (looks like ordering/annotation diff).

ben: quick diagnostic commands I ran locally:
```
# inspect manifest list
crane manifest gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321 | jq .manifests[].platform
# inspect digests
docker buildx imagetools inspect gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321 --raw
```

ben: root cause hypothesis: our multiarch push pipeline recently started producing manifest lists with platform entries in a different order (arm64 first vs amd64 first). cosign signs a particular manifestlist digest; the mirror/replicator computes a digest for the list it receives — ordering shift changes digest -> verification fails.

sre_jen: options are: 1) republish a canonical manifestlist with deterministic ordering and re-sign (preferred), 2) retag prev stable digest for canary to avoid blocking release window, or 3) patch replicator to normalize ordering on ingest (longer).

kyle: release window in 25m. we need decision fast — if we republish will that break existing digests?

ben: republishing will create a new digest (must re-sign). we can do a short lived plan: pin canary to previous digest (sha256:prev123) so deployments proceed, and do a follow-up republish+sign to restore provenance for the new tag.

Ali: I don't want to risk user-facing canary being different from what QA signed. proposal: hold canary promote for 30m, pin staging->canary to prev digest if any urgent bugs, and run a republish job that creates a deterministic manifestlist and signs it with cosign KMS key. notify compliance and add entry to release notes about re-signed image.

maya: I can run the republish script now. steps I'll run:
```
# rebuild manifestlist deterministic ordering
buildx imagetools create \
  --tag gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321-amd64 gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321-amd64@sha256:... \
  --tag gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321-arm64 gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321-arm64@sha256:...
# then sign
cosign sign --kms k8s://projects/redwood/keys/cosign-key gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321
```

ben: I'll coordinate the KMS sign and update the publish job to ensure platform entries sorted by arch name before pushing. also adding a unit test in the pipeline to fail on non-deterministic manifest ordering.

deploy-bot: staging pinned to digest sha256:prev123 by @Ali (hold flag set). canary promote suppressed.

Ali: plan ack — maya please run republish and ping here when cosign verify passes in eu-west1. if not fixed in 30m we'll fallback to pin canary (kyle will execute) and postpone canary release to next window.

kyle: acknowledged. I'll start rollback pin if we hit the 30m mark. :thumbsup:

maya: starting republish now, will post verification output in ~10m.

ben: I pushed a small helper to normalize manifest ordering in the publish job. PR #4387 incoming for review.

deploy-bot: verify result: cosign verify succeeded in us-central1 and eu-west1 for gcr.io/redwood/release:20260321 — provenance OK. staging->canary promote unblocked.

Ali: great, thanks everyone. I'll update release notes with a short blurb: "Republished and re-signed release:20260321 to ensure deterministic manifestlist ordering; no image contents changed."

maya: closing the hold now. moving the canary promote. :rocket:
